# Trade-off matrix

1. Write the decision as a question.
2. List two or three realistic options. Include "do nothing" or "change the configuration" when they are realistic.
3. Select the quality attributes that matter for this decision, for example performance, scalability, availability, consistency, security, cost, operability, team skills, and time to market.
4. Give each attribute a weight from 1 to 3. Give the reason for each weight.
5. Score each option from 1 to 5 for each attribute. Give the evidence or the label `ASSUMPTION:`.
6. Calculate the weighted totals. Do not let the total decide alone. Read the matrix for a fatal weakness.
7. Mark the decision: one-way door (difficult to reverse) or two-way door (easy to reverse).
8. Recommend one option. State what makes you change the recommendation.

## Output format

| Attribute (weight) | Option A | Option B | Option C |
|---|---|---|---|
| Performance (3) | 4 | 3 | 5 |
| Weighted total | | | |
